zh: 某个位置的水面高度由它左边最高柱和右边最高柱中较低的那个决定（两边的最高值都包含它自己），该位置的积水量等于这个高度减去自身高度。只看相邻柱子，或者取两侧较高的那堵墙，都会算错。
可以先求前缀最大值和后缀最大值数组再逐点求和；也可以只用两个指针从两端向中间走：哪一侧已知的最高值较小，那一侧下一根柱子的水位就已经确定了，因为另一侧已经有一堵不低于它的墙，中间未处理的柱子只会让另一侧的最高值更高。
令 left=0、right=n−1、leftMax=rightMax=0，答案用 64 位整数。当 left≤right 时：若 leftMax≤rightMax，先令 leftMax=max(leftMax, h[left])，答案加上 leftMax−h[left]，left 加一；否则对右侧做对称处理，right 减一。循环结束后输出答案。
en: The water level at a position is set by the lower of the highest bar on its left and the highest bar on its right (both maxima include the bar itself); the water there is that level minus the bar's own height. Looking only at adjacent bars, or taking the higher of the two walls, gives wrong answers.

You can build prefix-maximum and suffix-maximum arrays and sum point by point, or use two pointers moving inward from both ends: on whichever side the known maximum is smaller, the next bar's water level is already fixed, because the other side already has a wall at least that high and the unprocessed bars in between can only raise the other side's maximum.

Set left = 0, right = n-1, leftMax = rightMax = 0, and use a 64-bit answer. While left <= right: if leftMax <= rightMax, set leftMax = max(leftMax, h[left]), add leftMax - h[left] to the answer, and increment left; otherwise do the symmetric step on the right side and decrement right. Print the answer when the loop ends.

explanationEn:
## Source recovery and full range

The body of the fixed upstream fastprep/Zolostays/zolostays-trapping-rain-water.md is truncated at "Given n non-negative integers repres", so the width cannot be guessed from the remnant alone. Its starter explicitly hints "refert to LC42", the two complete input/output pairs are [0,1,0,2,1,0,1,3,2,1,2,1]->6 and [4,2,0,3,2,5]->9, and the full constraints match the official LeetCode 42. Following this explicit cross-reference, this site checked the official statement at https://leetcode.com/problems/trapping-rain-water/description/ and restored the missing definition: each bar has width 1, and the task is the total amount of water trapped after rain. This is not stitching rules together from a problem with the same name; it does not claim that the truncated raw text itself preserved the full body, and no upstream code was executed.

The full original range 1<=n<=20000, 0<=height[i]<=100000 is kept, without extending it to empty arrays. The standard input is adapted to n followed by n heights, separated by whitespace; the output is the total number of units of trapped water. The two original examples 6/9 are kept, and the third example [2,0,2]->2 is explicitly a supplement by this site. The maximum is reached by [100000,0,...,0,100000], which is 19998x100000=1999800000, so the original int return type is enough; the reference uses a 64-bit accumulator to express the sum clearly.

## Approach

The water a position can hold equals min(highest bar on the left, highest bar on the right) - the current bar's height (both maxima include the current bar). If there is no higher wall in one direction, the water flows out, so you cannot look only at the neighbors or take the larger of the two walls.

The reference processes from both ends toward the middle; leftMax and rightMax are the highest bars of the processed prefix and suffix, both initially 0. When leftMax<=rightMax, it processes the next bar on the left: if that bar exceeds leftMax, it holds no water and updates the left maximum; otherwise its water level is already bounded by the left maximum, and the right side already has a high enough wall, so it contributes leftMax-height[left]. The other case handles the right side symmetrically. This continues until every position has been processed.

## Proof of correctness

If leftMax<=rightMax and the current left bar is not higher than leftMax, then the processed right side has a wall of height rightMax (when leftMax=rightMax=0 the amount of water is 0 anyway), and the unknown middle positions can only increase the other side's maximum, never decrease it. Hence the smaller of the left and right maxima is determined to be leftMax, and the contribution of the current position is computed exactly. If the current left bar is higher than leftMax, then the highest value on the left including itself is its own height, so the position contributes 0 and updating leftMax is correct. The case where rightMax is smaller is fully symmetric.

Each round processes one previously unprocessed position, so nothing is missed or counted twice. The argument above shows that the contribution of every round is correct; at the end all positions have been processed, and the accumulated value equals the total amount of trapped water.

## Complexity

Reading the input and the two-pointer traversal are both O(n); storing the input array takes O(n), and the two pointers use O(1) extra space. The reference algorithm does not scan level by level over heights, so the full height 100000 and length 20000 are handled directly.

## Independent verification

The oracle builds complete prefix-maximum and suffix-maximum arrays and then sums point by point, without reusing the two-pointer state. On the small domain it also checks, level by level and cell by cell, whether each side has a wall reaching that level, counting the water cells directly; it exhaustively enumerates lengths 1..6 with heights 0..2 and actually runs the reference on each of them. The 163 unique oracle cases include the two original examples, this site's example, fixed-seed random cases, and boundaries. The official full-length cases cover zeros, a plateau at the maximum height, monotone sequences, a basin between two maximum-height walls, adjacent peaks and wide basins, multiple basins, and random heights; the largest basin is rechecked against the independent closed form 1999800000. Three wrong programs that exit normally - taking the larger wall, forgetting to subtract the bar height, and looking only at the immediately adjacent walls - are each run on all official cases, and their counterexamples are recorded.
